articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (July 21, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (July 21, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, July 21, 2026.
YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors
Featured news
How Karunya Gunavathy is helping women in Tamil Nadu transition from bidi rolling to sustainable livelihoods
Growing up in Tamil Nadu's bidi belt, Karunya Gunavathy watched women sacrifice their health to earn a living. Today, through the Kottravai platform, she is helping them transition from bidi rolling to sustainable livelihoods, with a mission to create jobs for 10,000 women.
Read more
Transition VC launches Rs 1,500 Cr Fund II
Transition VC, the Bengaluru-headquartered venture capital firm with a focus on the energy transition segment, has launched its second fund with a target corpus of Rs 1,500 crore. The VC firm plans to invest $2 million to $5 million each in over 20 engineering-led startups over four years, starting from the third quarter of the current fiscal.
Funding news
Traveltech startup 30 Sundays raises Rs 61 Cr led by Bessemer Venture Partners
Gurugram-based tech-enabled holiday planning and booking platform 30 Sundays has raised Rs 61 crore in a Series A funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from existing investors Info Edge Ventures and Eximius Ventures.
Suminter India Organics raises Rs 25 Cr debt from BlackSoil
Organic food ingredients company Suminter India Organics has raised Rs 25 crore in debt funding from BlackSoil Capital to strengthen working capital and support procurement during the peak harvest season. The company said the funding will help it source certified organic ingredients at scale while expanding engagement with its network of over 1 lakh smallholder farmers across India, the Philippines, and Africa.
Founded in 2004, Suminter operates an integrated farm-to-market platform covering sourcing, certification, processing, and global distribution of organic ingredients such as spices, cocoa, coconut products, and natural fibres. The company exports to leading food and ingredient brands across the United States, Europe, and other international markets while promoting regenerative farming and end-to-end traceability.
Zaggle to invest up to Rs 7.96 Cr in Unobanc
Spend management and SaaS fintech company Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services will invest up to Rs 7.96 crore in cross-border payments firm Unobanc Private Limited, which operates under the moneyHOP brand. Following the investment, Zaggle will hold up to a 19.9% equity stake in the company.
The move is aimed at expanding Zaggle's payments ecosystem and strengthening its presence in cross-border payments, remittances, and foreign exchange services for enterprise and retail customers. Unobanc, a subsidiary of Hop Financial Solutions, provides technology infrastructure for digital cross-border payments and has received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India for an Authorised Dealer Category-II licence to expand its forex and remittance offerings.
FireAI secures Rs 2.5 Cr from SucSEED Indovation Fund
Mumbai-based causal decision intelligence startup FireAI has raised Rs 2.5 crore from SucSEED Indovation Fund to accelerate its go-to-market strategy. The company will deploy 55% of the capital to expand its enterprise sales team and regional presence, while 35% will be invested in research and development to strengthen its AI platform. The remaining funds will support administrative operations and new office infrastructure.
FireAI's platform helps enterprises analyse complex business environments through anomaly detection, causal chain analysis, and conversational analytics in over 90 languages. The company said its technology enables business leaders to receive explainable, actionable insights by integrating directly with existing enterprise systems.
Khageshvara Aviation raises pre-seed funding
Deeptech startup Khageshvara Aviation Technology, which develops electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) cargo aircraft, has secured an undisclosed investment from Finvolve and India Accelerator as part of its ongoing pre-seed funding round. Existing investors including Rukam Capital, ACIC-VGU, and MIETY also participated.
The startup will use the funds to complete product development, accelerate field testing, build an interim cargo platform, and advance certification milestones. Founded in 2023, Khageshvara is developing indigenous cargo eVTOL aircraft with payload capacities ranging from 5 kg to 400 kg for defence logistics, emergency response, disaster relief, medical supply delivery, and remote connectivity in difficult terrains across India.
MS Dhoni invests in rooftop solar startup SolarSquare
Former India cricket captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni has invested in residential rooftop solar company SolarSquare through his family office, Midas Deals, as part of the startup's recently announced $53 million Series C funding round. Dhoni will also become the company's brand ambassador.
SolarSquare, which serves more than 50,000 homes across 29 cities, plans to use the capital to expand into 30-40 additional cities, strengthen its technology platform, enhance financing options and improve customer service.
The company provides end-to-end rooftop solar solutions, including consultation, installation, financing, and maintenance. The investment comes amid rising demand for residential rooftop solar driven by increasing electricity costs and greater consumer interest in clean energy.
Other news
IKEA to open second store in Delhi on July 30
IKEA India will open its second store in Delhi at DLF Avenue, Saket, on July 30, expanding its presence in the National Capital Region. Spread across 30,000 sq. ft., the store will offer nearly 3,000 products, with around 1,400 available for immediate takeaway, while customers can access IKEA's complete catalogue of over 6,900 products through its website, app and Shop by Phone service.
The company said the new outlet is designed to cater to households across South and Central Delhi with room displays and home furnishing solutions suited to urban lifestyles. Customers will also have access to planning, delivery, assembly, and installation services, along with an IKEA Café serving Swedish and local food.
Hyundai launches assistive technology startup programme
Hyundai Motor India Foundation, in partnership with AssisTech Foundation, has launched Samarth UnnATi, a startup scale-up programme to support assistive technology innovations in India. The initiative aims to help high-potential startups developing solutions for persons with disabilities through mentorship, capacity building, investor access, and ecosystem partnerships.
Hyundai's foundation has earmarked grant support of ₹75 lakh to facilitate market access and deployment of assistive technology products. The programme will also strengthen collaboration with disability welfare institutions and other stakeholders to promote wider adoption of accessible technologies. Hyundai said the initiative seeks to bridge the gap between innovation and accessibility while enabling startups to scale solutions that improve inclusion and independence for persons with disabilities.
NatWest, IIT Delhi launch fintech innovation programme
NatWest Group has partnered with IIT Delhi's Foundation for Innovation and Technology Transfer to launch the NatWest FinTech Frontier Program, an initiative aimed at accelerating innovation in banking technologies. The programme features separate tracks for researchers and startups, offering opportunities to develop and pilot solutions using NatWest's enterprise banking capabilities and real-world data. Selected participants will gain access to paid pilot projects and commercialisation opportunities in the UK banking market.
The collaboration will focus on artificial intelligence, intelligent automation, cybersecurity, digital trust, next-generation banking products, and quantum computing. NatWest said the initiative will strengthen collaboration between academia, startups, and industry to develop cutting-edge financial technology solutions.
Salesforce, REVA University launch AI-powered student platform
Salesforce has partnered with REVA University to launch REVAion, an AI-powered digital engagement platform aimed at enhancing the student experience from admissions to graduation. Built using Agentforce for Education, Agentforce for Marketing and Agentforce 360, the platform delivers personalised services across admissions, academics and campus operations. The initiative is part of REVA University's four-year digital transformation programme.
Salesforce said the collaboration also strengthens the university's Salesforce Centre of Excellence, which has trained more than 2,000 students in Salesforce technologies through specialised courses and faculty development programmes. The platform is designed to improve student engagement while equipping graduates with industry-relevant digital and AI skills.
Hitachi, GlobalLogic open smart building innovation hub in Noida
Hitachi Ltd., Hitachi Lift India and GlobalLogic have launched the BuilMirai Experience Centre at GlobalLogic's headquarters in Noida to showcase next-generation smart building technologies. The facility will serve as an innovation and customer engagement hub for Hitachi's BuilMirai digital services platform, which combines AI, building data and domain expertise to improve energy efficiency, sustainability and operational performance.
The centre will also support collaboration between engineers, customers, and industry partners to develop intelligent building management solutions. GlobalLogic will lead digital engineering efforts, while Hitachi Lift India will provide local operational expertise. Hitachi said insights generated through the centre will help accelerate the global deployment of its smart building solutions.
IndiaMART InterMESH reports 11% revenue growth in Q1 FY27
IndiaMART InterMESH reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹414 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, an increase of 11% from the corresponding period last year. Customer collections rose 8% year-on-year to ₹463 crore, while deferred revenue grew 16% to ₹2,014 crore. Net profit for the quarter stood at ₹172 crore, with cash flow from operations of ₹163 crore. The company ended the quarter with cash and investments of ₹3,553 crore. Standalone revenue increased 9% to ₹376 crore, while subsidiary Busy Infotech contributed revenue of ₹36 crore during the reporting period.
Ping Identity launches India data centre
Ping Identity has launched its India data centre capability, hosted on Google Cloud's Mumbai region, to help enterprises host identity workloads locally and comply with evolving data residency and privacy requirements. The company said the facility will reduce application latency, strengthen governance over digital identities, and support secure cloud identity adoption.
The deployment also enables organisations to improve consent management, access controls, and auditability while supporting AI applications and AI agents.
Ping Identity has an engineering centre in Bengaluru employing around 300 people. It said the data centre launch reflects its long-term investment in India's fast-growing digital economy and its commitment to supporting customers with locally hosted identity infrastructure.
Wipro Consumer Care to acquire Philippines personal care firm
Wipro Consumer Care International has signed a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of Philippines personal care company S Brands Consumer Care Inc. The acquisition, Wipro's 16th globally and second in the Philippines, strengthens its presence in Southeast Asia.
S Brands owns a portfolio of well-known products including KERATINplus hair treatment, AlcoPlus hygiene products, DeoPlus powder deodorants, Empress hair care, and Fiona Cologne. Wipro said the acquisition expands its personal care portfolio and reinforces its strategy of combining organic growth with acquisitions across Asia, the Middle East, and Africa. The company currently operates in over 60 markets and continues to build a portfolio of consumer brands.
CarDekho launches AI-powered employee engagement platform
CarDekho Group has launched Amber, an AI-powered employee listening platform designed to replace traditional annual engagement surveys with continuous, confidential feedback. The platform interacts with employees through channels such as WhatsApp and email during key milestones including onboarding, promotions and exits.
Amber uses artificial intelligence to analyse employee sentiment, identify recurring themes and flag emerging workplace issues in real time. Managers receive team-level insights, while HR leaders gain a live view of workforce engagement linked to retention, wellbeing and performance metrics. CarDekho said the platform reflects its AI-first strategy by extending AI beyond customer services to improve employee experience and organisational decision-making.
NetApp acquires AI infrastructure startup DataPelago
NetApp has acquired California-based AI data infrastructure company DataPelago to strengthen its enterprise AI capabilities. The acquisition brings DataPelago's GPU-accelerated data processing technology into NetApp's portfolio, enabling organisations to process data directly at the storage layer instead of transferring it to separate compute clusters.
According to NetApp, the technology can reduce infrastructure costs by up to 80% while delivering up to ten times faster performance for AI and analytics workloads. DataPelago's platform also eliminates the need for duplicate data copies, a major bottleneck in enterprise AI deployment. NetApp said the acquisition will help enterprises accelerate AI adoption while improving efficiency, scalability and data governance.
The Card Company launches premium prepaid metal card
The Card Company has launched what it claims to be India's first premium prepaid metal card powered by RuPay. Designed to make premium card benefits more accessible, the prepaid card does not require income-based eligibility or underwriting. Customers who complete KYC can activate a wallet and order the physical metal card by choosing a preferred feature plan.
The card offers benefits including global airport lounge access, complimentary buffet meals at select five-star hotels, buy-one-get-one coffee offers, and rewards in the form of gold coins redeemable as digital gold. The company said the product combines premium experiences with the flexibility of a prepaid payment instrument, targeting consumers seeking high-end lifestyle benefits without conventional credit card requirements.
GrowthX enters managed office space business
Commercial real estate advisory firm GrowthX has entered the managed office space segment with the launch of GO Office Workspaces. The company will invest over ₹8.6 crore to establish its first centre at Delphi Tower in Noida in partnership with ORD Group. Spread across 72,000 sq. ft., the facility will offer nearly 1,200 seats for enterprises, startups, multinational companies and global capability centres (GCCs). GrowthX plans to build a managed office portfolio of around 500,000 sq. ft. across the National Capital Region over the next 12-18 months before expanding to other metropolitan cities. The facility will feature enterprise suites, flexible workspaces and smart office infrastructure.
Mygate launches AI assistant for housing societies
Community management platform Mygate has launched MIRA (Mygate Intelligent Response Assistant), an AI-powered solution designed to automate financial and administrative tasks for resident welfare associations and housing societies. The platform can extract information from vendor invoices, reconcile payments, analyse transactions, monitor collections, and identify overdue accounts, significantly reducing manual work.
According to Mygate, pilot deployments showed treasurers and accountants reduced time spent on routine financial processes by up to 70%. Built into the Mygate platform, MIRA also enables committee members to obtain instant financial insights through natural language queries. The company said the solution aims to improve operational efficiency and financial transparency across residential communities.
Accenture appoints Pradeep Prabhala to lead India market
Accenture has appointed Pradeep Prabhala as the head of its India Market Unit, effective September 1, 2026. In his new role, Prabhala will work with clients to accelerate growth through data and artificial intelligence while supporting global organisations in establishing GCCs in India. He joins Accenture from McKinsey & Company, where he led the consumer sector in India and agriculture across Asia.
Prabhala has over two decades of experience in AI, enterprise transformation, supply chain, mergers and acquisitions, and sustainability. Accenture said the appointment reflects its continued investment in India as a strategic growth market and innovation hub.
IndiaMART's BUSY launches AI-powered MSME accounting platform
Busy Infotech, a subsidiary of IndiaMART, has launched BUSY Magic, an AI-powered accounting and business management platform for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The solution integrates accounting, billing, inventory, GST compliance and business reporting through a simplified interface designed for first-time software users and growing businesses.
BUSY Magic enables business owners to monitor sales, purchases, cash flow, receivables, payables, stock levels and e-invoices from a single dashboard. The company said the platform aims to help businesses transition from manual records and spreadsheets to connected digital workflows while reducing operational complexity through AI-driven automation and faster onboarding.
Deloitte India launches AI platform for SAP implementation
Deloitte India has introduced RapidAuto ConfigEngine (RACE), an agentic AI-powered platform that automates SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud configuration. The solution uses generative AI, specialised AI agents and Deloitte's proprietary SAP implementation assets to automate tasks ranging from capturing business requirements to configuring enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems.
Part of Deloitte India's INTEGRATE suite, the platform is designed to accelerate digital transformation by simplifying complex SAP implementations. RACE generates user stories, process blueprints, configuration plans and optimisation recommendations while helping organisations adopt fit-to-standard operating models. Deloitte said the platform enables faster, scalable and more efficient ERP deployments using AI-led automation.
GIFT City launches fintech startup acceleration programme
GIFT City has launched the Young Builders' Program under the GIFT International FinTech Innovation Hub in collaboration with the International Financial Services Centres Authority. The initiative aims to nurture the next generation of fintech startups by supporting entrepreneurs from ideation through commercialisation. Selected applicants will participate in a nationwide hackathon followed by an eight-week residential programme featuring mentorship from founders, investors, regulators and industry experts.
The top three startups will gain direct entry into the IFSCA FinTech Sandbox to test and validate their innovations in a regulated environment. GIFT City said the programme is intended to accelerate responsible fintech innovation and strengthen India's international financial services ecosystem.
Lawyered launches legal assistance plan for truck owners
Legal-tech platform Lawyered has introduced LOTS247 Sarathi, a digital roadside legal assistance plan for commercial vehicle driver-cum-owners. Priced at an introductory annual subscription of ₹999 per vehicle, the service combines legal assistance, compliance support and personal accident insurance. Subscribers receive 24x7 roadside legal support, telephonic legal advice, on-ground lawyer assistance during roadside incidents, challan resolution services, and compliance monitoring. The package also includes wallet credits worth Rs 1,100 that can be used towards challan-related convenience fees and select platform services.
Lawyered said the initiative aims to improve access to affordable legal protection and compliance services for India's commercial transport community.
Smarten Power sells 1.18 lakh units in Q1 FY27
Power backup and solar solutions company Smarten Power Systems sold around 1.18 lakh products during the first quarter of FY27, driven by strong demand for home UPS systems, solar power conditioning units, batteries and solar panels. The company attributed the growth to higher electricity consumption and elevated summer temperatures across northern India.
During the quarter, Smarten commissioned a 5,200 sq. ft. warehouse in Gurugram to strengthen its logistics network and added 32 new distributors across nine states. It also expanded its product portfolio with the launch of the HELIX 1100-1250 MPPT-based solar PCU series and two new battery models.
UPES Runway launches AI-focused startup pitching initiative
UPES Runway, the startup incubator of UPES, has launched the New Delhi leg of The Pitch 3.0, an initiative to identify and support AI-native and AI-driven startups across India. Seven shortlisted startups presented their ideas before investors and mentors after being selected from over 20 applications.
The startups span sectors including fintech, edtech, quantum computing, disaster management, image recognition, and deeptech. UPES plans to support 10 startups this year with funding of up to Rs 25 lakh, while exceptional AI-led ventures could receive up to Rs 50 lakh. The next edition of The Pitch 3.0 will be held in Bengaluru in September, targeting startups from southern and western India.
IIM Mumbai launches executive MBA in wealth management
The Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Mumbai has introduced a one-year executive MBA in wealth management in collaboration with Neo Wealth and Asset Management. Designed for working professionals in financial services, the weekend programme covers portfolio management, taxation, estate planning, behavioural finance and risk assessment.
The institute said the curriculum combines academic learning with practical industry insights through faculty-led sessions and practitioner interactions.
Alongside the programme, IIM Mumbai and Neo Wealth have signed an MoU to promote digital learning through masterclasses, research publications, case studies and industry content. The institute said the initiative aims to address the growing demand for specialised professionals in India's expanding wealth management industry.
Enlight Metals launches AI procurement platform
Enlight Metals has launched a Multi-AI Agent Procurement Platform to automate procurement and supply chain operations for manufacturing and steel companies. The company said the platform enables specialised AI agents to collaborate across procurement, logistics, inventory, finance, sales and customer support, helping businesses reduce manual processes and improve operational efficiency.
Designed for industrial enterprises, the platform delivers real-time information, automates workflows and supports faster decision-making by integrating multiple business functions. Enlight Metals said many manufacturers continue to rely on fragmented communication systems, resulting in delays and inefficiencies. The AI-powered platform aims to improve visibility across supply chains while enabling enterprises to make faster, data-driven procurement decisions.
Matrix Geo Solutions wins Central Railway contract
Matrix Geo Solutions Ltd. has received a letter of acceptance from Central Railway for conducting precision track geometry surveys covering more than 300 kilometres of railway lines. The project will use advanced geospatial technologies to assess and improve railway track alignment, supporting safer and more efficient train operations at speeds of up to 160 kmph.
The company said the technology will help identify alignment issues before they become safety risks, enabling timely maintenance and reducing long-term operational costs. The project is also expected to improve passenger comfort, strengthen railway asset management and support more effective maintenance planning across the rail network.

articles.title: This Nigerian founder has built AI-powered tools in the agri, ed-tech spaces - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian founder Juliet Chinenye Duru has designed and built two AI-powered tools from the ground up to solve real, tangible problems she observed in the Nigerian and African context.
AgriAI gives smallholder farmers a region-specific crop yield prediction and a concrete actionable recommendation, running on a cheap Android phone over a standard 3G connection.
NaijaLearn-AI, meanwhile, is a free multilingual AI tutor covering STEM and ICT topics in English, Pidgin, Yoruba, Hausa, and Igbo, accessible to students across all 250 and more Nigerian universities with no registration or paywall. Both tools are completely free to use.
“I handle everything from product design and engineering to deployment and research. My background as an ICT Lecturer and NLP/AI researcher meant I could move quickly from identifying the problem to shipping a working product,” Duru said.
She has certainly selected key issues to tackle. Nigeria loses an estimated NGN3.5 trillion annually to preventable crop failures, yet existing precision agriculture tools are built for high-bandwidth environments and expensive devices that most smallholder farmers simply cannot afford.
“There is no open, accessible, region-specific yield prediction tool built for the African farmer. For NaijaLearn-AI: mainstream AI tutors like ChatGPT or Khan Academy assume reliable broadband and English fluency, and none are calibrated for Nigerian university curricula or local languages. I spotted both gaps from direct experience and built the solutions myself,” said Duru.
The startup is currently self-funded and bootstrapped.
“As the sole founder and developer, I have been able to move fast and keep costs low,” Duru said.
“Both tools are newly-launched. The focus so far has been on getting the product right rather than aggressive marketing. NaijaLearn-AI is live and publicly accessible, and AgriAI is available on the Play Store. Early feedback from the developer and academic communities has been encouraging, and I am now shifting focus toward user growth.”

articles.title: Das Ende der Blackbox? Dieses KI-Modell soll autonomes Fahren sicherer machen
articles.text:
SafeDrive: So soll dieses KI-Modell autonomes Fahren sicherer machen
Ein Team von Forscher:innen um den Professor Jun Won Choi an der Seoul National University hat ein neues Modell für autonomes Fahren namens SafeDrive entwickelt. Dieses System adressiert die mangelnde Nachvollziehbarkeit bisheriger End-to-End-Ansätze, indem es Handlungsoptionen vorab auf ihre Sicherheit prüft.
Bisherige KI-Systeme ahmen menschliches Fahrverhalten meist nur auf der Basis gewaltiger Datensätze nach, können ihre konkreten Fahrmanöver im Zweifelsfall aber nicht logisch begründen. Wie in einem Fachartikel auf der wissenschaftlichen Plattform Arxiv nachzulesen ist, durchbricht die neue Architektur dieses tradierte Muster durch eine Technik namens Fine-Grained Safety Reasoning.
Die Software simuliert dabei parallel gleich mehrere mögliche Routen für die unmittelbare Zukunft und bewertet das jeweilige Kollisionsrisiko für jede einzelne dieser berechneten Trajektorien. Die Künstliche Intelligenz trifft somit keine unbegründeten Entscheidungen mehr, sondern wählt proaktiv den Fahrpfad mit dem höchsten statistischen Sicherheitswert aus.
Wie SafeDrive die Sicherheit beim autonomen Fahren erhöht
Auf technologischer Ebene setzt die Architektur auf zwei eng miteinander verknüpfte Netzwerke, um komplexe Verkehrsszenarien zu berechnen und spezifische Risiken zu quantifizieren. Das sogenannte Sparse World Network simuliert die zukünftigen Bewegungen anderer Verkehrsteilnehmer, während das „Fine-grained Reasoning Network“ die Einhaltung der befahrbaren Zonen auswertet.
Diese präzise Vorabkalkulation hat der wissenschaftlichen Arbeit auf der bedeutenden Fachkonferenz CVPR, die im Juni 2026 im US-amerikanischen Denver stattfand, eine Auszeichnung als Highlight-Paper eingebracht. Eine solche Ehrung erhalten jährlich nur rund drei Prozent aller Einreichungen, was die Relevanz der Untersuchung für die Automobilindustrie unterstreicht.
Wie The Next Web berichtet, signalisiert dieser akademische Erfolg zudem den wachsenden Einfluss Südkoreas im globalen Technologiewettbewerb. Der Staat untermauert damit seinen Anspruch, neben den etablierten Akteuren in den USA und China eine führende Rolle bei der Entwicklung zukunftsweisender Automobil-KI einzunehmen.
Die technischen Schattenseiten der erklärbaren Künstlichen Intelligenz
Trotz der offenkundigen architektonischen Vorteile bringt die simultane Berechnung diverser Trajektorien zwangsläufig einen deutlich erhöhten Bedarf an lokaler Rechenleistung mit sich. Wenn ein Fahrzeug in Bruchteilen einer Sekunde etliche Optionen durchspielen und bewerten muss, erfordert das extrem leistungsfähige und zugleich teure Hardware direkt im Auto.
Zudem weisen Fachleute zu Recht darauf hin, dass simulierte Sicherheitsbewertungen immer nur exakt so zuverlässig sein können wie die physische Sensorik, welche die rohen Echtzeitdaten liefert. Fällt die Umgebungswahrnehmung der Kameras und Radarsysteme durch widrige Wetterbedingungen teilweise aus, verliert auch der elaborierteste interne Erklärungsansatz seine fundamentale Datengrundlage.
In der Praxis äußern Beobachter wie Digital Trends in Kommentaren zu ähnlichen Systemen Bedenken, dass die Komplexität der Entscheidungsbäume zu unerwarteten Verzögerungen führen könnte. Eine „erklärbare Künstliche Intelligenz“ (XAI) muss erst noch beweisen, dass sie in echten Notsituationen nicht nur korrekte, sondern vor allem auch hinreichend schnelle Ausweichmanöver einleitet.
Dennoch bietet die gesteigerte Nachvollziehbarkeit entscheidende Argumente für Versicherungsgesellschaften und Regulierungsbehörden, die bei unvermeidbaren Unfällen nach juristisch verwertbaren Ursachen suchen. Wie TechXplore hervorhebt, entsteht durch diese Methode ein auditierbarer Entscheidungspfad, der den rein reaktiven Blackbox-Systemen gegenwärtig völlig fehlt.
Das südkoreanische Modell verbleibt erfreulicherweise nicht in der akademischen Theorie, sondern wurde bereits in ein kommerzielles Referenzmodell des Ministeriums für Handel, Industrie und Energie im südkoreanischen Sejong überführt. Erste lokale Automobilunternehmen testen die Software aktuell in realen Testfahrzeugen auf öffentlichen Straßen unter Alltagsbedingungen.
Die anstehende Erprobungsphase wird zeigen, ob sich dieser ressourcenintensive Ansatz gegenüber der etablierten Konkurrenz behaupten kann. Das Team von Entwickler:innen der Seoul National University plant nun, das System mit noch umfangreicheren Datensätzen für den regulären Serieneinsatz zu optimieren.

articles.title: Vigilancia 360° de alta resolución y sin pagar suscripciones: la Reolink OMVI 3i WiFi llega a España
articles.text:
A la hora de proteger la vivienda o el negocio con sistemas de videovigilancia, uno de los dilemas habituales es elegir entre una cámara de gran angular que cubra mucho espacio o una con movimiento pan-tilt que permita hacer zoom y seguimiento. Reolink busca resolver esta disyuntiva con la llegada a España de la OMVI 3i WiFi, una cámara de seguridad inteligente que destaca por su sistema de triple lente pensado para abarcar un campo de visión completo de 360º sin perder detalle.
Cámara de vigilancia Reolink OMVI 3i WiFi
Una cámara de vigilancia con la que no existen los puntos ciegos
El aspecto central de la OMVI 3i WiFi reside en la combinación de sus ópticas. Por un lado, integra un módulo panorámico de doble lente de 10 MP; por otro, suma una tercera lente PT (pan-tilt) de 8 MP. En conjunto, el sistema alcanza una resolución combinada de 18 MP, lo que le permite mantener una vista general y continua de la escena al tiempo que puede enfocar o realizar un seguimiento detallado sobre zonas o sujetos específicos.
Para sacar partido a esta estructura, esta cámara de vigilancia incorpora las tecnologías SyncTrack y Auto Framing. Estas funciones permiten que la cámara detecte, de forma automática, a personas u objetos en movimiento y los mantenga encuadrados y centrados en la imagen mientras se desplazan.
A nivel de software, el modelo estrena la tecnología IA ReoNeura, un sistema propio que realiza el procesamiento de detección inteligente y la búsqueda de vídeo directamente en el propio hardware. Al no depender de la nube para estas tareas de análisis, el equipo busca reducir tanto los falsos avisos como los tiempos de respuesta, reforzando además la privacidad de los datos.
En la misma línea, la propuesta de Reolink prescinde de las cuotas mensuales o servicios de suscripción obligatorios. Las grabaciones se pueden almacenar localmente mediante una tarjeta microSD de hasta 512 GB o conectando el equipo a un grabador NVR de la propia marca.
Precio y disponibilidad
La Reolink OMVI 3i WiFi ya se encuentra disponible en España con un precio oficial recomendado de 319,99 euros, pudiéndose adquirir tanto en la web oficial del fabricante como a través de su tienda en Amazon. Para quienes prefieran la instalación mediante cable de red en lugar de conexión inalámbrica, la marca también ofrece la versión OMVI 3i PoE.

articles.title: La nueva versión de X para Android ya está disponible: conoce qué cambia y qué fallos elimina
articles.text:
Los usuarios de Android ya pueden descargar una versión completamente renovada de la aplicación de X, antes conocida como Twitter. La compañía anunció el lanzamiento de una actualización que reconstruye la app desde cero con el objetivo de mejorar el rendimiento, corregir errores históricos y preparar la plataforma para la llegada de nuevas funciones en los próximos meses.
Según informó el equipo de ingeniería de X, la nueva arquitectura de la aplicación ofrece una experiencia más rápida y estable, con un desplazamiento más fluido del contenido, tiempos de carga optimizados y un sistema de notificaciones más confiable. La actualización ya está disponible a través de Google Play Store y puede instalarse como una actualización de la aplicación existente.
PUBLICIDAD
Una reconstrucción completa para mejorar el rendimiento
Durante años, la versión de X para Android fue objeto de críticas por parte de los usuarios debido a problemas de estabilidad y funcionamiento que persistían incluso antes de la compra de Twitter por parte de Elon Musk.
Mientras la aplicación para iPhone recibía mejoras frecuentes, la versión para Android acumulaba errores que afectaban la experiencia de uso, especialmente al navegar por el feed, abrir enlaces o recibir notificaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Con esta actualización, la empresa afirma haber dejado atrás esa base técnica para sustituirla por una nueva infraestructura desarrollada desde cero. El objetivo es facilitar el mantenimiento de la aplicación, acelerar el desarrollo de futuras funciones y reducir la aparición de errores.
Desde la cuenta oficial de ingeniería de X explicaron que la nueva arquitectura permitirá implementar novedades con mayor rapidez, además de ofrecer un funcionamiento más consistente en dispositivos Android.
PUBLICIDAD
Los errores que desaparecen con la actualización
Uno de los principales cambios está relacionado con la apertura de publicaciones compartidas desde otras aplicaciones.
Hasta ahora, era habitual que un enlace enviado por WhatsApp u otra plataforma no mostrara directamente el contenido esperado. En algunos casos la publicación nunca llegaba a cargar y, en otros, la aplicación redirigía al usuario al inicio de X en lugar de abrir el tuit específico.
PUBLICIDAD
Otro problema frecuente afectaba al sistema de notificaciones. Muchos usuarios recibían avisos correctamente en la versión web, pero nunca en el teléfono Android, provocando retrasos o la pérdida de información importante.
El feed también experimenta importantes mejoras. La pestaña “Para ti” podía quedarse bloqueada al iniciar la aplicación, obligando a actualizar manualmente la pantalla para que aparecieran nuevas publicaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, la pestaña “Siguiendo” cambiaba automáticamente entre el orden cronológico y el algoritmo de recomendaciones sin intervención del usuario, una conducta que generaba confusión y molestias. La compañía asegura que estos errores han sido corregidos gracias a la nueva estructura interna de la aplicación.
Una base preparada para las próximas funciones
Además de resolver problemas históricos, X considera que esta reconstrucción representa una inversión a largo plazo para el desarrollo de la plataforma.
Nikita Bier, jefe de producto de la compañía, calificó el proyecto como “uno de los mayores esfuerzos de ingeniería en la historia de X”. Según explicó, rehacer completamente la aplicación no solo mejora el rendimiento actual, sino que permitirá incorporar nuevas funciones con mayor rapidez en futuras actualizaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
La empresa sostiene que disponer de una arquitectura más moderna reducirá el tiempo necesario para lanzar herramientas y realizar ajustes sin afectar la estabilidad del servicio.
Las novedades que llegarán próximamente
Aunque la nueva aplicación ya introduce importantes mejoras, X confirmó que todavía quedan funciones pendientes para Android.
Entre ellas se encuentra una optimización adicional destinada a mejorar el rendimiento en teléfonos más antiguos, donde la experiencia todavía puede presentar limitaciones debido al hardware disponible.
PUBLICIDAD
También está prevista la incorporación de una compatibilidad más amplia con Espacios, la función de conversaciones de audio en directo que continúa expandiéndose dentro de la plataforma.
La hoja de ruta de la compañía incluye además un nuevo editor para crear reacciones en video, soporte para etiquetas de efectivo y la posibilidad de utilizar líneas de tiempo personalizadas, funciones que ya se encuentran en desarrollo.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo instalar la nueva versión
Los usuarios no necesitan descargar una aplicación diferente para acceder a estas mejoras. Basta con abrir Google Play Store, buscar la aplicación oficial de X y actualizarla a la versión más reciente si la actualización ya está disponible para su dispositivo.
Una vez instalada, todas las mejoras de rendimiento y correcciones de errores se aplicarán automáticamente sin necesidad de realizar configuraciones adicionales.
Con este rediseño, X busca reducir la brecha existente entre sus aplicaciones para Android y iPhone, ofreciendo una experiencia más estable para millones de usuarios que utilizan diariamente la red social desde dispositivos con el sistema operativo de Google. La compañía espera que esta nueva base técnica permita acelerar el desarrollo de futuras herramientas y responder con mayor rapidez a las necesidades de su comunidad.

articles.title: IPTV et streaming illégal : des milliers de sites sont tombés pendant la Coupe du monde
articles.text:
Alors que la Coupe du monde vient d’être décernée à l’équipe d’Espagne, les forces de l’ordre bouclent ce qui reste l’une des plus vastes offensives anti-piratage de l’histoire du sport. Menée par le ministère de la Justice américain et une foule de partenaires publics et privés (de la FIFA à beIN Media Group, en passant par Warner Bros ou encore l’UFC), l’opération visait à couper le robinet du streaming illégal. Et le moins qu’on puisse dire, c’est qu’ils n’ont pas fait les choses à moitié.
Carton rouge contre les sites pirates
Tout a commencé fin juin avec l’opération américaine « Offsides », qui visait d’abord un peu moins de 400 domaines web. Mais le coup de filet a vite pris une tout autre ampleur. En confirmant que ces plateformes retransmettaient les matchs en direct sans autorisation, les agents de l’HSI (pour « Homeland Security Investigations », qui font partie du service de l’Immigration et des Douanes des États-Unis) ont fait fermer plus de 1 000 adresses pendant la Coupe du monde 2026. À titre de comparaison, lors du Mondial 2022 au Qatar, « seulement » 78 domaines avaient été neutralisés.
Des chiffres impressionnants qui ont pu être obtenus grâce à une coopération de nombreux acteurs. En s’appuyant sur le réseau ICHIP, composé de procureurs spécialisés qui luttent contre la cybercriminalité et les infractions liées à la propriété intellectuelle à l’échelle mondiale, les enquêteurs ont ciblé des hubs bien connus du piratage, notamment en Bulgarie et au Pérou, tout en appuyant des actions en Colombie, en Pologne, en Roumanie ou en Croatie. De son côté, l’Alliance pour la créativité et le divertissement (ACE) a fourni plus de 3 000 pistes de sites suspects pour alimenter les saisies.
Arrestations, coupure des pubs et riposte des pirates
Du côté de l’Amérique latine, la réplique s’est organisée sous le nom de « l’Opération Carton Rouge ». Coordonnée par la Colombie avec huit autres pays comme le Brésil, l’Équateur ou l’Argentine, l’action a permis de bloquer 1 970 domaines et URL dans la région. Les autorités colombiennes sont également allées plus loin avec 15 arrestations. Parmi elles, quatre membres présumés du groupe « Los Ciberinfiltrados », accusés d’avoir piraté un opérateur télécom local depuis 2024 pour revendre des accès IPTV illégaux via des VPN et de faux identifiants.
Découvrez : 12 sites gratuits pour regarder des films et séries en streaming (légalement)
En parallèle du volet judiciaire, la guerre s’est aussi jouée sur le terrain financier. L’organisme TAG a ainsi coupé les revenus publicitaires de 1 376 sites spécialisés grâce à sa liste d’exclusion. De leur côté, les sites pirates ripostent déjà, avec de nombreux administrateurs qui ont rapidement basculé leurs plateformes vers des extensions iraniennes (.ir), beaucoup plus difficiles à atteindre pour la justice américaine.

Depuis son lancement en septembre 2023, le Bose QuietComfort s'est imposé comme le casque ANC “accessible” de la gamme QC, fort de ses 24 heures d'autonomie et d'une réduction de bruit saluée par la critique. Si les QuietComfort Ultra ont eu droit à leur deuxième génération dès septembre 2025, le QC standard, lui, semblait figé. Aucune fuite, aucune rumeur.
Mais voilà : le leaker billbil-kun, via Dealabs, lève le voile sur un potentiel Bose QuietComfort 2nd Gen dont la sortie serait programmée au 13 août prochain, avec une annonce officielle et des précommandes dès le 7 août.
Design repensé et audio spatial au programme
Le renouvellement irait bien au-delà d'un simple rafraîchissement cosmétique : les coussinets adopteraient une forme oblongue, dite “en pilule”, et le serre-tête s'élargit avec davantage de cuir synthétique pour gagner en confort.
Côté son, Bose introduirait sa technologie TrueSpatial, censée spatialiser l'écoute quel que soit le contenu, et ajouterait la prise en charge de l'audio sans perte via USB-C (un port jusqu'ici cantonné à la recharge sur le modèle sortant). Trois modes d'écoute remplaceraient l'ancien système personnalisable : Immersion, Cinema Mode (orienté vidéo) et ANC désactivé.
La technologie ActiveSense, elle, gagnerait en finesse pour lisser les pics sonores parasites en mode Aware.
L'autonomie, en revanche, ne bougerait pas : 24 heures avec la réduction de bruit, 18 heures avec le TrueSpatial activé. Six coloris accompagneraient ce lancement, dont cinq inédits : Blanc fumé, Mauve bois de rose, Vert eucalyptus, Menthe rosée et Taupe noisette, en sus du Noir reconduit.
Un positionnement tarifaire calculé
Selon les informations de Dealabs, le QC 2nd Gen serait commercialisé à 349,95 € en Europe, 299,95 £ au Royaume-Uni et 359 $ aux États-Unis. Le tarif européen se situe entre le prix de lancement du premier QC (399,95 €) et son prix actuel, tombé sous les 300 € après trois ans de décote.
Outre-Atlantique, le prix reste strictement identique à celui du modèle actuel, malgré l'ajout du TrueSpatial, du Cinema Mode et du son sans perte. Une grille qui trahit la volonté de Bose de maintenir le QC comme rempart abordable face à une concurrence ANC de plus en plus féroce.

articles.title: Police dismantle Kratos phishing platform, arrest developer
articles.text:
Authorities in Germany and the U.S. dismantled the central infrastructure of Kratos, a phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform with global reach, and its developer was arrested in Indonesia.
During the operation, authorities seized more than 200 servers, effectively disrupting the malicious service and rendering it inoperable.
The action was led by Frankfurt’s Prosecutor General Office (ZIT), Germany’s Federal police (BKA), which worked in collaboration with U.S. law enforcement agencies.
BKA’s announcement characterizes Kratos as “one of the world’s most widely used criminal phishing services,” with confirmed victims across 35 countries, particularly in Europe and the United States.
“Authorities believe that more than 1,800 criminal customers purchased Kratos and used it to conduct roughly 15,000 phishing campaigns per month,” BKA announced.
“Each campaign had the potential to affect several thousand recipients worldwide.”
The phishing toolkit, which allowed threat actors to create and manage fake Microsoft authentication pages, was rented to cybercriminals for phishing attacks.
The kit provided convincing login forms designed to steal email addresses and passwords, enabling the attackers to hijack Microsoft accounts.
Access to these accounts was often leveraged to “commit further crimes,” states BKA, hinting at post-compromise activity such as business email compromise, data theft, account takeover, and phishing attacks targeting the victims’ contacts.
The authorities estimate that the owner of the service made at least €300,000 ($342,000) since 2024, from subscription fees to the Kratos platform.
With the arrest of the technical administrator and the shutdown of key parts of its infrastructure, BKA states that these phishing campaigns can no longer continue.
A seizure banner was added to the service’s website, presenting the action as part of Operation Olympus Blade and stating that domain ownership has now been transferred to the FBI.
With the servers seized, authorities can further the investigation by retrieving new forensic evidence that may lead to the identification of customers of the service.

articles.title: Nvidia doubles down on AI factories as it showcases massive Vera Rubin performance gains - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia doubles down on AI factories as it showcases massive Vera Rubin performance gains
Artificial intelligence chip king Nvidia Corp. today revealed a fresh trove of performance benchmarks and architectural milestones for its next-generation Vera Rubin platform as it edges closer to global availability.
The new numbers are impressive, but on a higher level they also underscore the potency of Nvidia’s approach that combines custom silicon with its broader hardware ecosystem and aggressive software optimization to squeeze even greater efficiency gains for AI workloads.
The latest milestones showcase the effort the chipmaker has made toward fine-tuning its ecosystem to tackle the increased performance demands and exploding infrastructure costs of next-generation “agentic” AI workloads. It may be no accident that Nvidia is touting the wide range of its chips ahead of Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s annual product event in San Francisco Thursday, called Advancing AI.
Impressive gains
One of the key revelations came from Nvidia’s partner CoreWeave Inc., the neocloud company that provides rented, cloud-based access to its graphics processing unit platforms. In early production runs, CoreWeave showed that it was able to squeeze out an incredible 10 times more tokens per watt when running DeepSeek Ltd.’s R1 model on the new Vera Rubin platform, compared with the previous generation GB200 NVL72 system based on Blackwell.
It’s an impressive leap, but CoreWeave showed that the optimizations made to Vera Rubin can also be applied to the GB200 NVL72 system as well, improving throughput per megawatt by more than four times over a three-month span. Nvidia said these gains were validated across 250,000-plus distinct configurations and more than 1.4 million GPU hours of testing.
Nvidia also wheeled out some new numbers for its Vera central processing units for running autonomous AI agents that can perform work on behalf of humans with minimal supervision. The Vera CPUs were built on a custom microarchitecture specification code-named Olympus core, and are highly optimized to process the irregular control flows of AI agents. In the latest benchmarks, Nvidia demonstrated 1.9 times faster agentic performance and a six-fold improvement in latency over x86-based alternatives. The company also showed that Vera surpassed Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s flagship EPYC Turin CPU by almost 100% on selected industry benchmarks, underscoring the importance of custom silicon in eliminating CPU-side bottlenecks.
Infra optimizations
There’s no doubt that Nvidia’s processors are among the best in the business, but the company made it clear that these gains could only be achieved thanks to its strategy that’s focused on hardware and software co-design. The company also develops the required software and networking systems needed to optimize the performance of its chips so as to maximize power and cooling efficiency.
Nvidia revealed that by dynamically optimizing the full infrastructure and energy stack, it could deploy 40% more GPUs within the same power envelope. At the same time, it showed how it can also minimize the environmental impact of its new processors by cooling them in a 45°C closed-loop liquid-cooled system that saves about 4 million gallons of water per megawatt annually over standard cooling methods.
The company also talked about its latest generation of networking fabrics, showing how they continue to outperform the best generic Ethernet architectures. The sixth-generation NVLink 6 interconnect delivered 2.3 times higher simulated decode throughput for massive large language models than Ethernet-based networks.
Meanwhile, the company’s Spectrum-X platform enabled 1.6 times faster remote direct memory access bandwidth with 1.7 times fewer switches. This integrated network results in five times greater optical power efficiency and 10 times more reliability, Nvidia said. In particular, the company revealed, its latest Spectrum-X platform, Spectrum-6, is arriving at AI factories from the likes of CoreWeave, Microsoft Corp., Nebius B.V., SpaceXAI Corp. and Tesla Inc.
Nvidia is currently racing to ship the new Vera Rubin systems to customers and partners, including the likes of Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Meta Platforms Inc., Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Dell Technologies Inc., OpenAI Group PBC and CoreWeave. As those platforms inch closer to general availability, the release of the latest benchmarks is clearly a strategic move by Nvidia, aiming to show that it now has all of the pieces in the puzzle for its customers to build the “AI factories” of the future.
With reporting from Robert Hof

articles.title: Range Rover dévoile enfin son GT électrique et l’intérieur va faire jaser
articles.text:
Jusqu’ici, la famille Range Rover comptait quatre modèles : le Range Rover, le Sport, le Velar et l’Evoque. La marque britannique en officialise un cinquième, le Range Rover GT.
Le nom annonce la couleur : un grand tourer, cette catégorie d’autos taillées pour avaler les longues distances dans le confort, avec des proportions de coupé plutôt que l’allure d’un gros SUV. Martin Limpert, directeur de la marque Range Rover, le décrit comme « le Range Rover le plus proche d’une voiture jamais conçu, tout en restant indéniablement capable ». Comprendre : une auto qui privilégie la route, sans renoncer au tout-terrain maison.
Dans les faits, le GT sera le premier Range Rover 100 % électrique construit sur la nouvelle plateforme EMA (Electrified Modular Architecture), une architecture native en 800 volts pensée dès le départ pour l’électrique.
Il sortira des chaînes de Halewood, l’usine anglaise que JLR a convertie à l’électrique à coups de 500 millions de livres, soit environ 585 millions d’euros. À retenir tout de même : le GT démarre en tout électrique, une version hybride complète étant prévue plus tard dans sa carrière. Ce choix n’a rien d’anodin. Le CEO de JLR, PB Balaji, a reconnu que le groupe ajoutait une option hybride sur cette plateforme parce que l’adoption de l’électrique se révèle « plus lente que prévu ».
Où se glisse le GT dans la gamme ?
Le GT arrive au milieu d’une série de lancements électriques chez Range Rover. Il y a d’abord le Range Rover Electric, le vaisseau amiral dont on a déjà essayé les technologies très sophistiquées, puis le Range Rover Sport électrique et sa batterie de 118 kWh. Le GT, lui, ouvre une catégorie que la marque n’avait jamais explorée : le grand tourer électrique, taillé pour la route.
Là où le Range Rover Electric joue la continuité et prouve qu’il fait aussi bien que le thermique, le GT tente un positionnement inédit dans la gamme. L’appétit pour des Land Rover électriques est d’ailleurs tel qu’une entreprise française s’est lancée dans le rétrofit électrique du Defender.
Pour l’instant, on reste tout de même sur notre faim. Le communiqué s’attarde longuement sur le design : écran unique associé à un affichage conducteur, aération dissimulée sur toute la largeur de la planche de bord, tissu tissé qui masque les haut-parleurs, « sanctuaire de calme ».
La mécanique, elle, reste dans l’ombre. La puissance, l’autonomie, le prix et la date restent inconnus. Les prototypes roulent encore camouflés, en phase finale de test. On tient une mise en bouche alors que les chiffres sont promis pour plus tard cette année.
Sur le papier, l’intention se tient : élargir la famille Range Rover vers un modèle plus routier, au moment où JLR accélère enfin sur l’électrique après des années de retard. Tant que le constructeur garde les données techniques pour lui, on juge surtout une direction de style et une promesse. Le vrai bilan viendra avec la fiche technique complète, attendue plus tard cette année.

articles.title: L'astronaute française Sophie Adenot teste le robot de cuisine Food Processor à bord de l'ISS
articles.text:
Caviar d’aubergines et houmous. En ces temps de grosses chaleurs sur Terre, voilà de quoi se régaler sans trop de risque. Eh bien, c’est le menu concocté dans l’espace par Sophie Adenot. Le Cnes (Centre national d’études spatiales) raconte le 17 juillet 2026 comment l’astronaute française s’est mise à la préparation de bons petits plats grâce à un nouvel outil : Food Processor.
À première vue, l’appareil ressemble vaguement à un robot de cuisine tout ce qu’il y a de plus classique. Un bol pour mettre les aliments, quelques boutons, et ce qui ressemble à un moteur. Mais Food Processor est en réalité un peu plus que cela.
De la mousse au chocolat et du houmous cuisinés dans l’espace
L’enjeu est de concevoir un outil qui puisse être utilisé pour cuisiner lors de missions de longue durée, et ce avec des ingrédients qui pousseront directement dans l’ISS. Car s’il est assez facile de concevoir des aliments avec suffisamment de protéines pour tenir des mois, il faut aussi prendre en compte une contrainte : bien manger, c’est important.
Et pas seulement pour se nourrir, mais également pour le moral. Lorsque des astronautes se retrouvent à des centaines de milliers de kilomètres de chez eux, enfermés à plusieurs dans un espace extrêmement limité, et avec une notion très distante de ce qu’est l’intimité, il est important qu’ils puissent au moins se régaler avec des plats suffisamment variés pour ne pas trop s’ennuyer.
C’est là qu’intervient Food Processor. Il avait déjà été testé en 2023 par le Danois Andreas Mogensen, afin de réaliser une bonne mousse au chocolat. Ici, les recettes de Sophie Adenot se concentrent sur des ingrédients qui pourraient être produits directement dans l’espace. On retrouve donc de l’aubergine, des herbes aromatiques, et des pois chiches, ainsi qu’un peu de pâte de cacahuète.
Apprendre à cuisiner sans gravité
Conçu en collaboration avec Jean Hénaff, le groupe Andros (oui, ceux de « ça, c’est fort de fruit »), et l’agence Inneolab, cet engin a été d’abord testé lors d’une série de vols paraboliques en 0 g afin de s’assurer qu’il puisse fonctionner en apesanteur.
L’enjeu était notamment de faire en sorte que le bol soit bien hermétique, afin que les ingrédients puissent être mélangés à l’intérieur sans qu’ils se retrouvent à voler partout. Autant dire que les tests sur la mousse au chocolat étaient particulièrement… disons, graphiques, en vols 0 g.
Dans un robot classique, l’hélice qui mixe les ingrédients a tendance à les faire monter, sauf qu’ils retombent avec la gravité. Dans l’espace, cette règle ne s’applique pas et il a fallu imaginer une autre manière d’utiliser cette technologie.
Vient ensuite le moment du transfert, où il ne s’agit pas simplement d’ouvrir le bol, mais de placer une poche qui se fixe dessus pour que la préparation puisse être placée à l’intérieur, avant de finir dans une assiette.
En tout cas, pour l’instant le résultat est à la hauteur. Sophie Adenot a pu tester sa recette salée à deux reprises à bord de l’ISS, et devrait poursuivre par la suite avec sans doute d’autres ingrédients.

articles.title: Single-pass AI code isn't dead, but "high-reasoning" is the next frontier
articles.text:
Single-pass AI code isn’t dead, but “high-reasoning” is the next frontier
Ask an AI model what comes next after “bacon-double”, and the return is fairly unanimously “cheeseburger.” It’s a pattern-matched, single-pass output for the user, and it’s the one that we expect.
Above digital burger joint simplicity, we enter the world of high-reasoning, where multi-step problem-solving sees models execute chain-of-thought processes.
Going beyond a single pass is more akin to human reasoning, as it breaks down elaborate problems into more manageable, sequentially executed intermediate steps (with backtracks on errors) to provide an answer.
The trade-off is a higher volume of more complex code, which is harder to detect errors in at code review, but the model itself will typically perform better.
The question now becomes, when do we introduce (or perhaps even insist upon) high reasoning as part of the frontier model mix, and is it the next chasm to cross?
Relegating single pass to the simple end of the workload
CloudBees‘ CEO Moritz Plassnig tells The New Stack that single-pass AI coding is like “answering with the first thing that comes to mind” in the reasoning debate. That means it’s fine for simple problems, but not for ones with real depth or ambiguity.
Single-pass AI coding is like “answering with the first thing that comes to mind.”
“I don’t think single-pass is dead, but I do think it’ll be relegated to the simpler end of the workload,” Plassnig says. “What’s more interesting is teams routing work intelligently: lower-end models for boilerplate [routine predictable] tasks, but high-reasoning for anything architecturally complex or security-critical, rather than just treating ‘more reasoning’ as a universal upgrade.”
Plassnig confirms that he fully expects the “current trajectory of developers demanding more high-reasoning to evolve into the harness itself”, before those same software engineers then being happy to choose the right model for the task at hand.
“What’s interesting is teams routing work intelligently: rather than just treating ‘more reasoning’ as a universal upgrade.”
Sometimes the first response is the right one
General manager of ‘The Shop’ (a practical use case company division) at AI software operations engineering company Sparq, Jackson Stakeman, tells The New Stack that he’s somewhat (but not wholly) in consensus with CloudBees CEO Plassnig’s thoughts. Rather than defining single-pass AI coding as blurting the first thing that comes to mind, he defines it as “responding when you think you actually have something of value to add” to a query.
He reminds us that single-pass blurt or not, sometimes the first response is the right one, so pretending otherwise just adds cost and latency to problems that didn’t need it.
“That said, I agree that routing work intelligently beats treating more reasoning as a universal upgrade — I’d just frame where we are a bit differently,” Stakeman says. “We’re still early in AI adoption at enterprise scale. The simple workloads are the thick part of the bell curve, and the complex multi-agent orchestration tasks are the long tail. For companies that aren’t primarily technology businesses, but that use technology to drive value, what they mostly need from AI is for it to work.”
“We’re still early in AI adoption at enterprise scale. The simple workloads are the thick part of the bell curve, and the complex multi-agent orchestration tasks are the long tail.”
The catch is that the model becomes a black box
In his essentially practical, hands-on role, Stakeman underlines the fact that high-reasoning tools let organizations that never built strong prompt engineering skills skip that step, for a price.
“The catch is that the model becomes a black box,” he warns. “It might solve your problem, but it won’t tell you whether a custom orchestration would have solved it better. In the conversations we’re having with customers, it’s rare to hear about a custom LangChain-style build that’s actually kept pace with how fast the frontier models keep improving.”
He restates his view that frontier model labs seem to be moving faster than most in-house stacks can keep up. It’s a development that’s starting to force a financial conversation that’s only just getting going: real skepticism about whether the premium on models like GPT-5.6 Sol or Fable 5 are worth it for a given task.
As of now, OpenAI appears to talk more directly about “medium, max, and scientific” reasoning, rather than high reasoning, even in relation to GPT-5.6 Sol. In a somewhat similar vein, Anthropic talks about chain-of-thought faithfulness when discussing why reasoning models don’t always say what they think.
“In our view, the deciding factor isn’t really the model; it’s whether a team has a clear way to measure ROI on AI spend. Teams with that mechanism can experiment and compare a cheap, fast model against a high-reasoning one, task by task. Teams without it tend to default to whatever’s marketed as ‘best’, and those are exactly the teams most likely to get steered away from high-reasoning the moment the bill comes due. Not because it’s the wrong tool, but because they can’t prove it is the right one,” Stakeman clarifies.
High reasoning is not rocket science, or FrontierMath
By way of clarification, high reasoning is not the same as FrontierMath, but there is a degree of overlap between these two occasionally connected cousins.
OpenAI commissioned Epoch AI to produce 300 math questions for the FrontierMath benchmark, which the nonadvocacy research nonprofit confirmed at the start of 2025. In terms of use, FrontierMath can act as a benchmark for evaluating advanced mathematical reasoning in AI of the type that features high reasoning.
What do developers think of high-reasoning? It might still be early days; there’s precious little ascerbic commentary out there just now.
That may be down to the still-emerging nature of these functions, or it could be because “high-reasoning” is sometimes used to describe governmental policymaking and even Machiavellianism.
What (arguably) matters most in the immediate months (and yes, this is AI, so it could be weeks or days) ahead is how well enterprise organizations are able to assess any given AI tool for its worth. That measure of worthiness comes down to correctness and effectiveness, multiplied by cost and divided by its ability to integrate and orchestrate before it attempts to accelerate and (dare we even say the word?) innovate.

articles.title: 'To grow a platform like ours, you have to have exclusive games and services' — Xbox execs confirm Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution 'are just the first' exclusive Xbox titles, but 'large live-service titles' will be multi-platform
articles.text:
'I can assure you, Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution are not the only titles we're planning' — Xbox's chief strategy officer confirms the company wants to make more exclusives, but 'large live-service titles' will be multiplatform going forward
Xbox wants a "reliable pipeline" of exclusive games
- Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball confirms Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution "are just the first" exclusive Xbox titles
- Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty says, "There has to be a reason for people to buy an Xbox"
- Ball says this plan doesn't mean every Xbox single-player game will be console exclusive
Xbox has confirmed that the Microsoft-owned company is looking to expand its console-exclusive portfolio, and Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution won't be the only two exclusives coming to Xbox consoles and PC.
During the Xbox Games Showcase 2026 last month, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced that The Coalition's next Gears of War game will be an Xbox console exclusive, meaning the game won't be coming to PlayStation 5.
Later, Clockwork Revolution, inXile Entertainment's steampunk role-playing game (RPG), will also drop PS5 and launch exclusively on Xbox Series X, Series S, and PC.
Xbox began exploring multi-platform a few years ago, but amidst Microsoft's major Xbox restructuring, which included mass layoffs of 3,200 people, and what Sharma is calling a "reset" of the business, it seems things are reverting to the way things used to be with an emphasis on console exclusivity.
According to Xbox chief content officer Matt Booty, who discussed the matter with GamesRadar, "There has to be a reason for people to buy an Xbox," and console exclusives can act as "a reward" for players.
Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball also confirmed that Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution won't be timed exclusives, unlike games like Starfield, but "permanent ones," and the company is looking to embrace exclusivity more.
"I can assure you, Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution are not the only titles we're planning," Ball said. "To grow a platform like ours, you have to have exclusive games and services. These are not going to be the only two titles."
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Ball added that "large live-service titles" will be multiplatform moving forward, but suggested that this won't mean every Xbox single-player game will be console exclusive.
For instance, Fable will launch on PS5, Xbox and PC on the same day, along with Halo: Campaign Evolved, which is the first Halo game to ever release on PlayStation.
"I wouldn't overly fixate on single-player," he said. "I think that's a good rule of thumb, but it certainly isn't something that's carved in stone."
The executive explained that Microsoft has a "framework" for deciding which games will be exclusive and which ones will be multiplatform and recognizes "this approach is not obvious to all of our players, and we are committed to making this clearer."

articles.title: SMIC's third-gen 7nm node shows smaller metal pitch than Intel 18A, higher transistor density than TSMC N6 without EUV — analysis of N+3 shows significant advancement for Chinese semi manufacturing
articles.text:
SMIC's third-gen 7nm node shows smaller metal pitch than Intel 18A, higher transistor density than TSMC N6 without EUV — analysis of N+3 shows significant advancement for Chinese semi manufacturing
But its transistor density is well behind 18A's.
An analysis of Huawei's Kirin 9030 system-on-chip (SoC) for smartphones conducted by SemiAnalysis revealed that SMIC's third-generation 7nm-class fabrication technology (N+3) has smaller metal pitch than Intel's 18A fabrication technology and that China's leading foundry has managed to achieve transistor density on par with manufacturing process that rely on EUV lithography. But does this make SMIC's N+3 node as competitive as Intel's 18A or TSMC's N2 and N3? Not really.
SemiAnalysis' teardown indicates that SMIC's N+3 fabrication process supports a minimum metal pitch of 32.5nm, which is nominally tighter than the approximately 36nm pitch used for many high-performance cells in Intel's Panther Lake CPU, even though 18A can support approximately 32nm metal pitches. The video from SemiAnalysis and High Yield does not reveal other important characteristics of SMIC's N+3, such as contacted gate pitch (CGP), standard cell height (tracks or nm), or fin pitch, so we cannot make direct comparison of this node to Intel's or TSMC's technologies. What it does reveal is estimated transistor density of around 113.4 million transistors per square millimeter (Mtr/mm2), which is even higher than transistor density of TSMC's N6, 107.7 Mtr/mm2.
TSMC's N6 uses multiple EUV layers, so achieving higher transistor density without using EUV lithography is an indisputable technological achievement of SMIC. The foundry achieves this density by using DUV multi-patterning, including self-aligned quadruple patterning on the tightest layers, and extensive design-technology co-optimization (DTCO). In addition, SemiAnalysis believes that SMIC used techniques like reduced fin counts, placing contacts directly over active gates, and tightening cell isolation. Such methods allow for increased transistor density, but at the cost of increased process complexity, cost, yield risks, and design constraints.
Meanwhile, transistor density does not equal overall process competitiveness. Despite its compact layout, the Kirin 9030 reportedly delivers performance comparable to flagship application processors from roughly three years ago and has a substantial energy-efficiency disadvantage compared with modern Apple, Qualcomm, MediaTek, and Samsung designs. Huawei's highest performing CPU core is characterized as roughly Cortex-X2-class in IPC, while Apple's much smaller efficiency cores reportedly outperform it in integer workloads and consume considerably less power.
Given the fact that Kirin 9030 is neither a performance nor efficiency champion, the provocative comparison with Intel 18A is not exactly justified. Although SMIC N+3 has 32.5nm minimum metal pitch that is nominally tighter than the approximately 36nm pitch used in Panther Lake, 18A offers both higher transistor density and considerably higher performance efficiency. In addition, 18A uses gate-all-around transistors and backside power delivery, which make it particularly suitable both for mobile SoCs and for data center applications.
SemiAnalysis concluded that while export restrictions have slowed China's technological progress, progress is still being made. SMIC could potentially continue increasing density by tightening upper and lower metal layers, shorter standard cells, smaller gate pitches, and eventually backside power delivery. If the company continues scaling, N+4 could approach TSMC N5-class density, while N+5 with backside power might reach Intel 18A-class density, according to SemiAnalysis. Still, transistor density alone does not necessarily bring substantial improvements of performance or power efficiency.

articles.title: Fire departments are testing autonomous drones that fight wildfires before crews even arrive
articles.text:
Forward-looking: As wildfires grow larger each year, fire departments and other organizations are seeking new tools to support firefighters' efforts. Several US departments are exploring autonomous drones, which could enable new, more flexible strategies for extinguishing smaller fires before they become more serious.
A California company recently began demonstrating a system that allows firefighters to direct autonomous drones to combat wildfires. While departments already use observation drones, deploying them to fight fires directly remains an unexplored tactic.
Unmanned drones do not have anywhere near the range or water-carrying capacity of water bomber aircraft used to combat large fires, but they could help contain potentially dangerous blazes soon after they are spotted. That crucial early phase is the focus of Seneca's next-generation UAS system.
The San Francisco company recently drew the attention of fire services in California, Montana, and Utah with a system that directs a squadron of five firefighting drones with minimal human intervention. Each drone carries about 100 pounds of water or fire retardant and has a round-trip range of up to 10 miles. The range can extend to 20 miles, depending on the distance between the fire and the drone's base station.
Once cameras, lookout sensors, or a 911 caller detect a fire, firefighters can upload a GPS waypoint to the drones via an app and launch them from a towed platform. While firefighters do not steer the drones directly, they can tell them where to fly and which areas to avoid. The drones reach an average speed of around 30 mph and fly a few dozen feet above the ground – high enough to avoid ground obstacles but low enough to avoid interfering with air traffic.
When the drones arrive, they attack the blaze in succession before returning to base. There, a single technician can refill each drone, swap in a freshly charged battery, and prepare it to return to the fire within minutes. Once firefighters arrive at the scene, they can determine whether subsequent attack runs are necessary.
Seneca designed the drones to extinguish fires at the highest risk of becoming serious within 10 to 15 minutes of their initial discovery, which is often the most crucial window for stopping them from spreading. The system is also far cheaper than scrambling helicopters and can reach difficult, steep terrain more easily than firefighters can.
Meanwhile, XPRIZE recently held a competition focused on designing firefighting drone systems. Former US Fire Administrator Dr. Lori Moore-Merrell noted that the technology represents an inflection point that public policy, supply chains, and operational standards must catch up with.

articles.title: NVIDIA Shows DLSS 5 Progress and Technical Details at SIGGRAPH 2026
articles.text:
Tuesday, July 21st 2026
	
		
	
		
	
	NVIDIA Shows DLSS 5 Progress and Technical Details at SIGGRAPH 2026
NVIDIA has once again showcased its DLSS 5 neural rendering at the SIGGRAPH 2026 event, currently taking place in Los Angeles. Despite the initial negative reaction from gamers, NVIDIA is continuing to develop the technology, offering improvements and a new demonstration of how DLSS 5 is intended to function. One of the most interesting aspects is that game developers can choose from three DLSS 5 models, each providing a different level of structural intensity, global illumination, texture detail, and more. These models, labeled Model A, Model B, and Model C, can be tailored to specific scenes or character needs, allowing developers to mix and match according to their requirements. Each model carries a different parameter count, meaning that some are more compute and memory-intensive than others. However, they generally fit and run fine on a single GPU without any problems.
Another noteworthy feature is the preservation of artistic intent, which was heavily criticized in the original DLSS 5 demo. Each individual object, scene, and game setting can be customized according to the developer's vision. This is one of the challenges NVIDIA faced with DLSS 5, as maintaining visual identity, object semantics, and character poses, along with output lighting semantics, motion, and art direction, is crucial. Within these strict parameters, DLSS 5 applies material photorealism to enhance visual appeal. Below you can even see the customization of the applied model, where there are adjustable parameters that can be done per scene and per character.The second challenge that the company faced is temporal streaming. Traditional generative AI video generators process in chunks, reasoning across a frame and generating a batch of frames at once. However, real-time rendering requires immediate generation, frame by frame. Since DLSS 5 uses motion vectors from the game engine, it can generate additional textures instantly, without delay. This results in no shimmer or image corruption, as DLSS 5 know exactly where to attach itself and perform its texture generation instantly.The final challenge for DLSS 5 is speed. To render a 4K frame with 8.3 million pixels at over 60 FPS, NVIDIA achieves this in less than 16 ms, with most of the processing time consumed by the game engine rather than the DLSS 5 model. The model is so efficient that users will not notice any delay during gameplay, and it operates on a single GPU. While NVIDIA highlights VRAM efficiency, it remains unclear whether 4K gaming will be limited to high VRAM GPUs or something else. As the launch is expected this fall, the company will provide general system requirements and further details, but the improvements compared to the original demo seem promising for now.
